title: Phoenixville football rallies late to win at Pottstown
summary: A fourth-quarter touchdown pass gave the Phantoms a 26-21 win Friday night, their third straight, evening their record at 4-4 and setting up a likely battle for second place in the PAC Frontier at Pottsgrove next week.

title: Spring City Hotel restaurant reopens Sunday under new management
summary: The Diable family has taken over the long-running restaurant at 88 N. Main St., with chef Tim Diable writing a new menu. A grand reopening is set for Sunday, Oct. 18 at 3 p.m., and the kitchen is still hiring.

title: Pottstown's 2027 budget draft carries a tax hike of about 6%
summary: Borough staff showed council two versions of a $64.4 million budget: one with a 5.89% tax increase that holds library funding flat, and one at 6.42% that grants the library its full 20% request.

title: Route 23 Wawa near Phoenixville sets an Oct. 22 grand opening
summary: The long-debated 24-hour Wawa with 10 fuel pumps replaces the former Exxon at 799 Valley Forge Road in Schuylkill Township. Doors open at 8 a.m. Thursday, with free coffee through Oct. 25.

title: Pottstown remembers Bill Krause, organizer of its July 4th parade
summary: The longtime Phillies Fire Company driver and former borough councilman died Oct. 12 at 90. He ran the July 4th committee for 28 years and founded the New Year's Day Polar Bear Plunge at Riverfront Park.

title: Pottstown council approves twin homes for the burned-out church lot
summary: Council voted 5-2 to let a developer build three sets of twin homes where Transfiguration Lutheran Church burned last November, attaching 17 conditions that must be met before construction starts.
loc: Former Transfiguration Lutheran Church site, Pottstown

title: $1 million state grant kicks off an all-abilities playground at Sanatoga Park
summary: Lower Pottsgrove broke ground on Adventure Grove, a $1.6 million inclusive playground that will replace the park's 23-year-old play equipment. Volunteers have been pushing for the project since 2019.

title: Neighbors raise money for a Phoenixville family displaced by fire
summary: A stove fire on Oct. 5 left an east-end apartment on Kenalcon Drive uninhabitable, and a GoFundMe is collecting help for the mother and daughter who lived there. The fire marshal believes the cause was accidental.

title: Chocolate & Coffee Festival returns to the Oaks expo center Oct. 24-25
summary: The third annual Pennsylvania Chocolate & Coffee Festival brings more than 150 vendors to the Greater Philadelphia Expo Center, with live coffee roasting, maker demos and a four-foot chocolate sculpture marking America's 250th.

title: Whole Foods, L.L. Bean and Barnes & Noble headed to Upper Providence's District at Black Rock
summary: A 148,000-square-foot retail center on the former Quest Diagnostics campus off South Collegeville Road is about 89% pre-leased as construction starts, with Toll Brothers adding 122 townhomes next door. Completion is targeted for late 2027.
loc: 1201 S. Collegeville Rd, Upper Providence (near Oaks)
